source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Chemistry (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring; stems restated in our own wording, no solution content by policy. Numbering runs continuously 1–68: VSAQ 1–21 (21 entries), SAQ 22–64 (43 printed numbers, 50 entries after splitting 43 into a–d and 45 into a–e), LAQ 65–68 (4 entries), plus INTEXT SOLVED PROBLEMS 5.1–5.13 (13 printed labels, 19 entries after splitting 5.1, 5.5 and 5.9) = 94 entries; problems 5.1, 5.10 and 5.11 repeat VSAQ 12–14, SAQ 44 and SAQ 46 with slightly different data. The odd scan pages 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, 67 and 69 are cropped at the left margin (the 'A)' markers are cut), so an asterisk before 29, 41, 53, 54, 64, 5.5, 5.6, 5.11 or 5.12 may have been lost; scan page 56 shows a sliver of printed page 59 along its right edge.

questions.stem: Define a system. Give an example.
A system has an adiabatic wall and ΔU = W_ad. What does this tell you about the heat and the work with respect to the system?
A system loses an amount of heat q, and no work is done on the system. What type of wall does the system have?
What is the work done in the free expansion of an ideal gas, in a reversible process and in an irreversible process?
In the equation ΔU = q − p_ex ΔV, what is the value of ΔU when the volume is held constant?
In the isothermal free expansion of an ideal gas, find the values of q and ΔU.
In an isothermal irreversible change of an ideal gas, what is the value of q?
In an isothermal reversible change of an ideal gas, what is the value of q?
State the first law of thermodynamics.
What are the sign conventions for work done on the system and for work done by the system?
What are the sign conventions for heat q when heat is transferred from the surroundings to the system, and when heat is transferred from the system to the surroundings?
No heat is absorbed by the system from the surroundings, but work w is done on the system. What type of wall does the system have?
No work is done on the system, but heat q is taken out of the system by the surroundings. What type of wall does the system have?
Work is done by the system and heat q is supplied to the system. What type of system is it?
What are the sign conventions for ΔH in exothermic reactions and in endothermic reactions?
Give the equation that relates ΔU and ΔH.
What is the relationship between Cp and Cv?
A decrease in enthalpy is not the criterion for spontaneity. Why?
Explain the relationship between the Gibbs energy change and the equilibrium constant.
If ΔH° and ΔS° are measured, it is possible to estimate ΔG°. Is this true? Why?
State the third law of thermodynamics.
What are open, closed and isolated systems? Give one example of each.
Define state function and state variables. Give examples.
'Internal energy is a state function.' Explain.
'Work is not a state function.' Explain.
What is heat? Explain.
Derive the equation for W_rev in an isothermal reversible process.
Explain the state function enthalpy, H. What is the relationship between ΔU and ΔH?
Show that ΔH = ΔU + Δn(g) RT.
questions.notes: The asterisk before 29 is partly cut by the left-margin crop of scan page 59; read as one star.

questions.stem: Explain extensive and intensive properties.
Define heat capacity. What are Cp and Cv? Show that Cp − Cv = R.
What is the enthalpy of a reaction? Explain the standard enthalpy of a reaction.
Define and explain the standard enthalpy of sublimation.
Define and explain the standard enthalpy of formation, ΔfH°.
Define and explain the enthalpy of combustion, ΔcH°.
Define and explain the enthalpy of atomisation, ΔaH°.
Define and explain bond enthalpy, ΔbondH°.
What is the bond enthalpy of the C–H bond in CH₄?
Define heat of solution, ΔsolH°, and heat of dilution.
Explain the spontaneity of a process.
What is entropy? Explain with examples.
Can ΔU and ΔS distinguish between irreversible and reversible processes? Explain.
Does the entropy increase in the following process? A liquid evaporates to vapour.

questions.stem: For the oxidation of iron, 4Fe(s) + 3O₂(g) → 2Fe₂O₃(s), the entropy change is −549.45 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ at 298 K. Although the entropy change is negative, the reaction is spontaneous. Why? ΔrH° = −1648 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.
questions.notes: Same question as problem 5.10, which prints the entropy change as −549.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: The sign and magnitude of the Gibbs energy change of a chemical process tell about its spontaneity and about the useful work that can be extracted from it. Explain.
In a process, 701 J of heat is absorbed by a system and 394 J of work is done by the system. What is the change in internal energy for the process?
questions.notes: PRINTED TYPO in the working below the question: the work is once written as 304 J; the question datum is 394 J.

questions.stem: The reaction of cyanamide(s) with dioxygen was carried out in a bomb calorimeter, and ΔU was found to be −742.7 kJ mol⁻¹ at 298 K. Calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction at 298 K. NH₂CN(s) + (3/2) O₂(g) → N₂(g) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l).
questions.notes: Printed 'for the reaction of 298K'; read as 'at 298 K'.

questions.stem: Calculate the number of kJ of heat needed to raise the temperature of 60.0 g of aluminium from 35 °C to 55 °C. The molar heat capacity of aluminium is 24 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
The enthalpy of combustion of carbon to CO₂ is −393.5 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate the heat released when 35.2 g of CO₂ is formed from carbon and dioxygen gas.
The enthalpies of formation of CO(g), CO₂(g), N₂O(g) and N₂O₄(g) are −110, −393, 81 and 9.7 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively. Find the value of ΔrH for the reaction N₂O₄(g) + 3CO(g) → N₂O(g) + 3CO₂(g).
Given N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g); ΔrH° = −92.4 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the standard enthalpy of formation of NH₃ gas?

Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of CH₃OH(l) from the following data: CH₃OH(l) + (3/2) O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l), ΔrH° = −726 kJ mol⁻¹; C(graphite) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔcH° = −393 kJ mol⁻¹; H₂(g) + (1/2) O₂(g) → H₂O(l), ΔfH° = −286 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.notes: The stem prints the methanol state as 'CH₃OH(1)' (digit one) where the equations use (l).

questions.stem: Calculate the enthalpy change for the process CCl₄(g) → C(g) + 4Cl(g), and calculate the bond enthalpy of C–Cl in CCl₄(g). ΔvapH°(CCl₄) = 30.5 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔfH°(CCl₄) = −135.5 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔaH°(C) = 715.0 kJ mol⁻¹, where ΔaH° is the enthalpy of atomisation, and ΔaH°(Cl₂) = 242 kJ mol⁻¹.
For an isolated system, ΔU = 0. What will ΔS be?

For the reaction 2A + B → C at 298 K, ΔH = 400 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = 0.2 kJ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. At what temperature will the reaction become spontaneous, taking ΔH and ΔS to be constant over the temperature range?
For the reaction 2Cl(g) → Cl₂(g), what are the signs of ΔH and ΔS?
For the reaction 2A(g) + B(g) → 2D(g), ΔU° = −10.5 kJ and ΔS° = −44.1 J K⁻¹. Calculate ΔG° for the reaction and predict whether the reaction can occur spontaneously or not.
The equilibrium constant for a reaction is 10. What will be the value of ΔG°? R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T = 300 K.
State the first law of thermodynamics. Explain its mathematical notation.
State the second law of thermodynamics and explain it.
Explain Gibbs energy.
Explain the spontaneity of a process in terms of Gibbs energy.
State and explain Hess's law of constant heat summation.
Explain the experiment used to determine the internal energy change of a chemical reaction.
Explain the experiment used to determine the enthalpy change of a chemical reaction.
Explain the spontaneity of a reaction in terms of the enthalpy change, the entropy change and the Gibbs energy change.
